header.stance: 油價與工廠需求走強，使聯準會升息預期提前

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

油價反彈、美國製造業報告走強，使6月1日短天期公債殖利率明顯上升，扭轉前一交易日通膨壓力暫緩的行情。2年期殖利率上升7個基點至4.05%，10年期升2個基點至4.47%，30年期則維持4.99%。能源成本增加，訂單與生產又保持強勁，交易員因而提早預期聯準會下一次升息的時間。

美伊停止交換訊息的報導，最初引發較全面的債券賣壓。之後美方的外交說明帶動部分回升，但WTI收盤仍上漲5.49%至$92.16。10年期名目殖利率的升幅，完全來自通膨補償增加，較長天期實質殖利率則未改變。

利率壓力並未使企業融資停擺。高收益債發行迎來五週最忙碌的一天，一家遭降評的業務發展公司擴大售債，收購及AI融資案也開始尋找買家，股市同樣上漲。但對能源進口國而言，油價與美元同步走強，使政策更難抉擇，尤其歐洲與亞洲部分經濟活動已顯疲弱。

## 油價與工廠需求，使聯準會升息預期提前

傳出德黑蘭暫停與華府交換訊息後，美國公債各天期殖利率一度上升5至9個基點。隨後美方表示，以色列與真主黨已同意停止攻擊，與伊朗的談判也仍在進行，債券才收復部分跌幅。WTI仍上漲5.49%至$92.16，Brent上漲3.18%至$94.98，週五支撐債市的能源降價利多隨之逆轉。

美國工廠的表現，也讓市場難以相信通膨會很快回落。ISM製造業指數升至54.0，高於預期的53.2。新訂單由54.1升至56.8，生產由53.4升至54.3，就業雖由46.4改善至48.6，仍低於景氣擴張門檻。供應商交貨指數維持60.6，價格指數則僅由84.6降至82.1，仍處於極高水準。

另一項製造業PMI終值由54.5升至55.1，顯示產出成長為2022年4月以來最快，成本壓力再起、交貨嚴重延遲，企業也持續累積庫存，出口卻連續第十一個月偏弱。對債市而言，內需生產強勁與供給摩擦的影響，蓋過了就業及出口較弱的部分。

營建活動較不一致。4月支出增加0.4%，年化金額達$2.1724兆，高於公布前預測的0.1%，但官方估計的信賴區間為正負0.7個百分點。私人住宅支出增加0.8%，私人非住宅支出下降0.2%；製造業營建支出月減1.2%，較一年前減少18.5%。住宅投資的表現，優於企業建設活動。

交換市場已完全反映2027年3月前升息一次，最快於10月行動的機率約50%。2年期殖利率收高7個基點至4.05%，5年期升5個基點至4.18%；10年期僅升2個基點至4.47%，30年期維持4.99%。殖利率曲線因此趨平，2s10s利差收窄5個基點至42個基點，2s30s收窄7個基點至94個基點。

10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.4%，抗通膨公債實質殖利率則維持2.07%。5年期實質殖利率升3個基點至1.64%，7年期升2個基點至1.85%，20年期與30年期分別持平於2.49%及2.71%。市場上調較近的政策利率路徑，並未要求長期實質利率再提供額外補償。2s5s10s蝶式利差上升1個基點至負16個基點，2s10s30s下降3個基點至負10個基點，也反映各天期走勢不同。

國庫券同樣重新定價。13週與26週券的附息等值殖利率各升3個基點至3.71%及3.78%，4週與8週券各升1個基點。美國財政部標售$890億91天期國庫券，最高得標貼現率3.630%、投標倍數2.69倍；另標售$770億182天期券，得標貼現率3.665%、投標倍數2.84倍。新券已完成標售，之後仍有交割。

最高法院審理總統Donald Trump試圖免除聯準會理事Lisa Cook職務的案件之際，前主席Jerome Powell就央行獨立性提出警告。他表示，若容許總統因政策分歧撤換官員，將摧毀維持經濟穩定所需的公信力。即使經濟放緩，這種制度變化仍可能推高通膨預期，以及投資人持有長債所要求的補償。

股市繼續走高，S&P 500上漲0.26%、Nasdaq 100上漲0.60%、半導體指數上漲1.06%，受惠於AI獲利與投資預期。大型科技公司規劃的資本支出最高達$7,250億，未來可能改善生產力，但首先會增加晶片、電力、營建與融資需求。

其他市場較為謹慎。VIX上升4.77%至16.05，美元指數上漲0.29%至99.2。槓桿基金、資產管理機構及其他投機帳戶持有約$165億美元多頭部位，三週前約為$50億。黃金則下跌1.87%至$4,475.20。股票與美元走強、波動率上升、黃金轉弱，顯示投資人對同一波能源及政策衝擊，採取了不同的資產配置反應。

## 利率提高，借款人仍能再融資

高收益債借款人當日發行$55億債券，為五週以來最多，即使上市信用債基金隨利率上升而下跌。LQD跌0.39%、HYG跌0.59%、JNK跌0.62%。已完成及正在籌備的融資金額，更直接呈現借款人取得資金的情況。

FS KKR Capital原先至少尋求$4億，最終發行$9億高收益債，訂單達$15億，定價殖利率7.5%，落在最初約7%中段至高段討論區間的下緣。這家業務發展公司因貸款減記及股利削減，先後被穆迪與惠譽降至非投資等級；KKR近期已提供$3億特別股資金，以及$1.5億股票收購要約。

貸款資產品質雖惡化，股東支持與定價仍促成發行，所得款項可能用於再融資。今年業務發展公司已籌資逾$140億，其中超過$55億是在4月該市場重新開放後取得，較好的融資環境也有利這家面臨挑戰的借款人。

銀行團開始銷售QXO Building Products的$30億高收益債，以取代收購TopBuild所用的過橋融資，另搭配$30億定期貸款。債券分為2031年及2034年到期兩部分，各$15億。貸款初步討論為基準利率加225個基點，價格99至99.5，支應約$170億收購價的一部分。併購融資供給有限，有助吸引買家，但對景氣敏感的建材業務仍須承擔新增槓桿與整合風險。

Elk Grove Village Property尋求發行$8.5億高收益債，支應芝加哥地區一座完全租給CoreWeave的資料中心，租期15年、對應約$22億收入。款項將償還$5億既有債務及利息，並支付剩餘工程。與AI基礎設施有關的企業，今年已發行近$270億風險較高債券。長約提供收入能見度，工程完工、單一承租人及再融資風險仍是信用判斷重點。

貸款供給不足，也幫助借款人降低成本。Restaurant Brands Europe、nexeye及Parts Holding Europe要求將既有歐元貸款利差下調25至50個基點，背景是歐洲今年發行量約比去年少8%，折合$1,248億。Citadel Securities則銷售2033年到期的$42.5億貸款，初始利差200個基點、價格99.5至99.75，將原本2031年到期的$39.5億貸款展期，並增加$3億借款。

Atalian需要的不只是時間，還包括股權改組。這家法國設施管理公司有€9.19億債券將於2028年到期，持有約60%債券的投資人同意透過重整取得控制權。約三分之二負債將轉為多數股權，其餘債務延至2031年，投資人另承諾最多€1.4億新超優先順位融資。與財務較健全、或得到較強支持的借款人相比，Atalian無法只靠再融資或利差調整解決問題。

主權債權人也對減債條件有分歧。持有尚比亞$13.6億、2053年到期美元債逾25%的投資人，反對前一期提過的買回要約。提前參與者每$1,000面額可取得$780，之後為$740；若75%持有人接受，剩餘債券清理條款便可能在票息由0.5%升至7.5%之前，強制處理未參與者的債券。反對者的持有規模，使這個門檻，以及未來票息調升的價值如何分配，成為焦點。

對一般再融資成本偏高的國家，債務交換提供另一途徑。Enosis希望擴大以較好條件置換主權債、再將節省資金用於環境或社會項目的交易，取得Legal & General五年$10億承諾。可能符合條件的債務超過$1兆，但2021年以來完成的私人資本交易僅約$60億。潛在市場很大，實際執行規模仍相當有限。

## 能源進口國在通膨與成長轉弱之間取捨

歐洲央行執委Isabel Schnabel表示，伊朗戰爭已不能再被視為短暫能源通膨，基礎設施與供應鏈受損，正使壓力擴散到商品價格與預期。她支持升息，但對之後的政策路徑仍持審慎態度。

歐洲工廠的數據呈現這項困境。5月歐元區製造業PMI終值由52.2降至51.6，產出指數由52.3降至51.3，新訂單停滯、出口下降、就業萎縮。投入成本卻以2022年5月以來最快速度增加，出廠價格通膨也達三年半高點。經濟活動正在走弱，傳到客戶端的價格壓力反而加重。

中期消費者預期稍有改善。4月三年期通膨預期由3%降至2.9%，一年期維持4%，五年期維持2.4%，仍高於歐洲央行目標。這讓官員多一些謹慎行動的空間，但未能消除能源與供應鏈成本持續偏高的疑慮。

英國房市已承受房貸成本的壓力。Nationwide平均房價5月下跌0.6%至£27萬8,024，為今年首次下降，也比經濟學家預期的0.2%跌幅更大，年增率放緩至1.7%。平均兩年期固定房貸利率仍為5.68%，比2月下旬高近0.9個百分點，市場同時完全反映年底前英國央行升息一次。Nationwide認為，若能源價格恢復正常，房市疲弱可能只是短暫現象；後續交易將顯示，需求延後有多少來自不確定性，又有多少出於融資成本。

日本創紀錄的匯市干預，仍未克服美日利差。隔夜指數交換反映近期升息機率約78%，油價提高進口帳單，日圓偏弱則使通膨壓力延續。本國公債殖利率更有吸引力，也可能降低日本投資人對匯率避險後外國債券的需求。

企業投資卻不像獲利那麼強。日本扣除軟體的資本支出較前季下降3.5%，包含軟體則與去年同期持平，低於預期的成長4%；同期間營收增加1.1%，經常利益增加14.6%。有獲利的企業似乎仍在延後投資承諾，若地緣政治不確定性持續、貨幣政策又收緊，國內需求將面臨風險。

南韓試圖從債券供給減輕壓力。自5月18日起，財政部官員每日與交易商及資產管理機構通話；10年期殖利率升至2023年末以來最高後，政府將6月規劃發債量削減約21%。美國收盤後公布的5月CPI年增率，卻由2.6%加速至3.1%，高於預期中位數2.9%，核心通膨也達2.5%。當局力圖穩定融資環境之際，燃料與旅遊成本正使價格壓力擴大。

較早公布的中國製造業調查提供部分相反訊號。PMI由52.2降至51.8，出口走弱，投入及產出價格通膨均放慢，與歐洲、美國重新升高的供應鏈價格壓力不同。

印度更直接面對能源、匯率與財政風險。伊朗戰爭爆發以來，10年期主權債殖利率上升約34個基點至7%，5年期債券因市場預期緊縮而跌得更多。盧比貶值、大量進口石油推高成本，燃油與肥料補貼又增加政府籌資需求。Kotak Mahindra估計，稅收不足與補貼增加，可能使財政赤字從預算目標的GDP占比4.3%擴大至4.6%，較不利情境下甚至達4.8%。

部分經理人預期，本輪可能升息75至100個基點，5年期交換利率自衝突開始後已上升逾60個基點。其他投資人則認為，供給型衝擊下不宜貿然緊縮，以免傷及轉弱的需求。看法分歧，使短中期債券特別容易受到油價持續性與匯率政策影響；預算成本則將壓力延伸至更長天期政府借款。

土耳其的成長放緩，讓取捨更為尖銳。第一季GDP較前季僅增0.1%，低於所有預測，也不及前季的0.4%；年增率由3.4%降至2.5%。但央行已因能源及食品成本，將年底通膨目標由16%調高至24%。單憑成長轉弱，仍不足以支持更寬鬆政策。

智利則顯示，油價展望改變可以很快影響投資部位。較早對協議的樂觀預期，使長期損益兩平通膨率與主權風險指標回到接近戰前水準，並吸引買家轉向短天期披索名目債券。偏好1至5年期抗通膨工具的投資人占比，由一個月前72%降至接近54%。停止談判的消息及油價反彈，使這項調整受到考驗，關鍵在燃油與消費物價轉嫁有多快。

哥倫比亞選舉帶來相反走勢。右派政治素人Abelardo de la Espriella在首輪取得43.7%選票，領先左派Ivan Cepeda的40.9%，兩人進入第二輪。美元債全曲線上漲，披索大升3.6%，創四年來最大單日漲幅，交換利率則下跌。投資人期待較親市場的政策及對石油開發的支持。這項政治風險重新定價，與整體外部環境形成對照：美國殖利率、美元及油價上升，對美元債與能源進口國不利，EMB下跌0.44%。

## 前瞻市場意涵

6月2日JOLTS、6月3日ISM服務業、6月4日初領失業救濟金與修正後生產力，以及6月5日就業報告，將顯示製造業強勢是否延伸至其他部門。職缺、聘僱與自願離職反映勞動需求，服務業就業及價格則可對照工廠調查。非農就業、失業率、薪資與單位勞動成本，有助區分持續的需求壓力，以及製造業就業分項已呈現的疲弱。需求與服務價格若仍強，2年期及5年期將繼續承受升息提前的風險；若普遍降溫，投資人便有理由回補部分週一賣壓。

油價仍是更即時的波動來源。荷莫茲海峽出口若能穩定恢復、油價持續下降，將降低通膨補償，讓央行更有餘裕等待；若再度受阻，能源進口國的匯率與債券曲線將繼續承壓。6月5日印度央行、6月10日至11日歐洲央行，以及6月16日日本央行決策，將顯示官員如何區分短暫能源成本與更廣泛的物價上漲，也可觀察各國回應是否進一步強化美國市場已反映的緊縮預期。

供給則提供融資環境的實際考驗。美國財政部6月3日進行長天期買回，6月4日接續短端現金管理買回及附息公債供給公告；QXO貸款與債券融資預計在6月2日至3日推進。若訂單接近初步條件、國庫券穩定、交割有序，將顯示借款人仍可在新的利率水準再融資。若企業需要大幅讓利，或3、10與30年期供給公告前後長債再度偏弱，則可能反映投資人及交易商的承接能力更吃緊。

overall_summary.headline: 能源與工廠價格重燃通膨風險，短期美債領跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
2年期美國公債殖利率上升7個基點至4.05%，10年期僅升2個基點至4.47%，30年期維持4.99%。美伊停止交換訊息的報導推升油價，之後的外交說明只使債券部分回升；WTI收漲5.49%至$92.16。10年期名目殖利率的升幅來自通膨補償，較長天期實質殖利率則持平。

美國製造業加重了利率壓力。ISM升至54.0，訂單與生產走強，價格指數仍高。交換市場已完全反映2027年3月前升息，10月行動的機率約50%。AI相關預期支撐股市，但波動率與美元也上升。

借款人繼續找到買家，高收益債發行合計$55億，FS KKR擴大售債，QXO及一座與CoreWeave有關的資料中心開始銷售新債。較弱借款人需要重整，尚比亞則遇到足以使剩餘債券清理門檻受到關注的反對勢力。海外能源成本升高，但歐洲工廠活動、日本投資及土耳其成長轉弱，使政策選擇更難。接下來的勞動及服務業數據，將顯示美國製造業的價格壓力是否更為廣泛。
overall_summary.summary: 油價上升、製造業強勁，使市場提早預期聯準會升息，2年期殖利率升幅遠大於長端。企業發債仍活絡，能源進口國則更難兼顧通膨與經濟成長。

section_summaries.summary: 油價反彈、美國工廠走強，帶動前端領跌的美債行情。企業融資與股市仍具韌性，能源進口國卻在部分活動轉弱之際，再度面對通膨壓力。

section_summaries.section_title: 油價與工廠需求，使聯準會升息預期提前
section_summaries.summary: 外交消息僅帶來部分回穩，油價仍大漲。訂單與生產強勁，使升息預期提前，推升短中期實質殖利率及通膨補償，長期實質殖利率則持平。

section_summaries.section_title: 利率提高，借款人仍能再融資
section_summaries.summary: 遭降評的業務發展公司擴大售債，收購與AI借款人尋求融資，貸款稀缺也支持利差重訂。Atalian須債轉股並取得新優先融資，尚比亞買回案則遭一批債權人反對。

section_summaries.section_title: 能源進口國在通膨與成長轉弱之間取捨
section_summaries.summary: 歐洲工廠放緩、成本上升，凸顯政策兩難。英國房市、日本投資及土耳其成長提供謹慎理由，印度油價與補貼負擔則影響財政前景。哥倫比亞受選舉結果帶動上漲。
美國勞動與服務業數據將考驗升息提前的定價，能源流量及海外央行決策仍是近期風險。美國財政部操作與QXO融資，則可觀察新供給在較高利率下如何成交。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Oil's rebound and a stronger US factory report sent short Treasury yields sharply higher on June 1, reversing the previous session's tentative inflation relief. The 2-year yield rose 7 basis points to 4.05%, while the 10-year added 2 to 4.47% and the 30-year held at 4.99%. Traders moved toward an earlier Fed increase as energy costs rose alongside firm orders and production.

Reports of a break in US-Iran exchanges initially drove a broader bond selloff. Later diplomatic reassurance brought a partial recovery, but WTI still ended 5.49% higher at $92.16. At 10 years, rising inflation compensation accounted for the entire nominal-yield increase; longer-term real yields were unchanged.

The pressure on rates did not shut corporate borrowers out. High-yield issuance reached its busiest day in five weeks, a downgraded business-development company enlarged its bond sale, and acquisition and AI financings sought buyers. Equities advanced too. For oil-importing economies, however, higher energy costs and a firmer dollar made policy choices harder just as parts of Europe and Asia were showing weaker activity.

## Oil and Factory Demand Bring Fed Tightening Closer

Treasury yields initially rose between 5 and 9 basis points after reports that Tehran had suspended message exchanges with Washington. Bonds recovered some ground when the US said Israel and Hezbollah had agreed to halt attacks and talks with Iran were continuing. The recovery was incomplete: WTI rose 5.49% to $92.16 and Brent gained 3.18% to $94.98, reversing the energy relief that had supported Friday's market.

US manufacturers supplied a second reason to question how quickly inflation would ease. The ISM manufacturing index rose to 54.0, above a 53.2 consensus. New orders increased to 56.8 from 54.1 and production to 54.3 from 53.4. Employment improved to 48.6 from 46.4 but remained below the expansion threshold. Supplier deliveries held at 60.6, while prices slipped to 82.1 from 84.6—still an exceptionally high reading.

The separate final manufacturing PMI increased to 55.1 from 54.5. It showed the fastest output growth since April 2022, renewed cost pressure, severe delivery delays and inventory building, alongside an eleventh month of export weakness. Stronger domestic output and supply friction outweighed the softer employment and export details in the bond market.

Construction was more uneven. April spending rose 0.4% to a $2.1724 trillion annualized rate, above a 0.1% pre-release forecast, although the official confidence interval was plus or minus 0.7 percentage point. Private residential outlays increased 0.8%, while private nonresidential spending fell 0.2%. Manufacturing construction declined 1.2% on the month and 18.5% from a year earlier. Housing investment held up better than business building activity.

Swaps fully priced a hike by March 2027 and assigned roughly a 50% chance to a move as early as October. The 2-year yield closed 7 basis points higher at 4.05%, with the 5-year up 5 at 4.18%. The 10-year's 2-basis-point rise to 4.47% and the unchanged 30-year at 4.99% left the curve flatter: 2s10s narrowed 5 basis points to 42, and 2s30s fell 7 to 94.

The 10-year breakeven rose 2 basis points to 2.4%, while its TIPS yield held at 2.07%. Real yields increased 3 basis points at five years to 1.64% and 2 basis points at seven years to 1.85%; the 20- and 30-year readings stayed at 2.49% and 2.71%. Investors marked up the nearer policy path without demanding a fresh concession in long-term real rates. The 2s5s10s butterfly rose 1 basis point to -16 and 2s10s30s declined 3 to -10, consistent with the different moves along the curve.

Bills also repriced. Coupon-equivalent yields on 13- and 26-week paper rose 3 basis points to 3.71% and 3.78%, while 4- and 8-week yields added 1 basis point. Treasury awarded $89 billion of 91-day bills at a 3.630% high discount rate and 2.69 bid-to-cover, and $77 billion of 182-day bills at 3.665% with 2.84 cover. The auctions cleared the new supply, with settlement still ahead.

Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell addressed the central bank's independence as the Supreme Court considered President Donald Trump's effort to remove Governor Lisa Cook. Allowing presidents to dismiss officials over policy disagreements would destroy the credibility needed for stable economic outcomes, he warned. Such a change could raise inflation expectations and the compensation investors demand on long bonds, even in a slowing economy.

Stocks continued to rise. The S&P 500 gained 0.26%, the Nasdaq 100 0.60% and the semiconductor index 1.06%, supported by AI earnings and investment expectations. Large technology companies' planned capital spending of as much as $725 billion could eventually improve productivity, but first creates demand for chips, power, construction and financing.

Other markets were less sanguine. The VIX rose 4.77% to 16.05 and the dollar index gained 0.29% to 99.2. Leveraged funds, asset managers and other speculative accounts held about $16.5 billion of long-dollar positions, up from roughly $5 billion three weeks earlier. Gold fell 1.87% to $4,475.20. The combination of stronger stocks and dollar exposure, higher volatility and weaker gold showed investors responding differently to the same energy and policy shock.

## Borrowers Refinance Despite Higher Rates

High-yield borrowers sold $5.5 billion of notes on the busiest day in five weeks, even as listed credit funds fell with the rate selloff. LQD lost 0.39%, HYG 0.59% and JNK 0.62%. The volume of completed and proposed financing gave a more direct account of borrowers' access to capital.

FS KKR Capital sold $900 million of junk bonds after initially seeking at least $400 million. Orders reached $1.5 billion, and the notes yielded 7.5%, the low end of initial discussion in the mid- to high-7% range. Moody's and Fitch had cut the business-development company to junk after loan write-downs and dividend reductions. KKR had recently supplied $300 million of preferred equity and a $150 million share tender.

Sponsor support and pricing helped the sale despite the deterioration in the loan book. Proceeds may refinance debt. Business-development companies had raised more than $14 billion during the year, including over $5.5 billion since the segment reopened in April, providing a more constructive financing backdrop for the challenged issuer.

Banks began marketing $3 billion of QXO Building Products junk notes to replace a bridge used for the TopBuild acquisition, alongside a $3 billion term loan. The bonds comprise two $1.5 billion tranches due in 2031 and 2034. Initial loan discussions were around 225 basis points over the benchmark at a price of 99 to 99.5, funding part of a roughly $17 billion purchase. Limited M&A supply could help draw buyers, although the transaction adds leverage and integration risk to a cyclical building-products business.

Elk Grove Village Property sought $850 million of junk bonds for a Chicago-area data center leased entirely to CoreWeave for 15 years, representing about $2.2 billion of revenue. Proceeds would refinance $500 million of existing debt and interest and fund the remaining construction. Companies tied to AI infrastructure had already raised nearly $27 billion in riskier bonds during the year. The long lease offers revenue visibility, with construction completion, a single tenant and refinancing still central to the credit assessment.

Scarcity was also helping loan borrowers reduce costs. Restaurant Brands Europe, nexeye and Parts Holding Europe sought cuts of 25 to 50 basis points on existing euro loans. Year-to-date European issuance was about 8% below the previous year at $124.8 billion equivalent. Citadel Securities marketed a $4.25 billion loan due in 2033 at an initial 200-basis-point spread and a price of 99.5 to 99.75. It would extend a $3.95 billion facility due in 2031 and add $300 million of borrowing.

Atalian needed a change of ownership as well as more time. Holders of about 60% of the French facilities-management company's €919 million of notes due in 2028 agreed to take control through a restructuring. Roughly two-thirds of liabilities would convert into majority equity, remaining debt would extend to 2031, and investors committed up to €140 million of new super-senior financing. The arrangement contrasts with the refinancings and repricings available to healthier or better-supported borrowers.

Sovereign creditors also disputed the terms of reducing debt. Holders of more than 25% of Zambia's $1.36 billion 2053 dollar bond opposed the tender described in the previous edition. The offer pays $780 per $1,000 for early participation and $740 later. With 75% acceptance, a cleanup call could remove remaining investors before a possible coupon increase from 0.5% to 7.5%. The size of the opposing group brought that threshold, and the allocation of the potential step-up's value, into focus.

Debt swaps offered another route for countries facing expensive conventional refinancing. Enosis aimed to expand transactions that refinance sovereign debt on better terms and direct savings to environmental or social projects, supported by a $1 billion, five-year commitment from Legal & General. More than $1 trillion of debt may qualify, but only about $6 billion of private-capital transactions had been completed since 2021. The financing has considerable potential reach, with execution so far much smaller than the eligible market.

## Oil Importers Weigh Inflation Against Weaker Growth

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said the Iran-war shock could no longer be treated as temporary energy inflation. Damage to infrastructure and supply chains was spreading pressure into goods prices and expectations. She supported an increase while remaining cautious about the path afterward.

Europe's factories illustrated the dilemma. The final euro-area manufacturing PMI fell to 51.6 in May from 52.2, with output slowing to 51.3 from 52.3. New orders stagnated, exports declined and employment contracted. Yet input costs rose at the fastest pace since May 2022, and output-charge inflation reached a three-and-a-half-year high. Activity was weakening while the price pressures reaching customers intensified.

Consumer expectations were somewhat more reassuring at the medium horizon. Three-year inflation expectations eased to 2.9% in April from 3%, while one-year expectations stayed at 4% and the five-year measure held at 2.4%, above the ECB's target. The improvement gave officials some room for caution without resolving concerns over persistent energy and supply-chain costs.

In Britain, mortgage costs were already weighing on housing. Nationwide's average price fell 0.6% in May to £278,024, the first decline of the year and larger than economists' 0.2% forecast. Annual growth slowed to 1.7%. The average 2-year fixed mortgage rate remained 5.68%, almost 0.9 percentage point above late February, while markets fully priced one BOE increase by year-end. Nationwide said the weakness could be short-lived if energy prices normalized; subsequent transactions would show how much demand had been delayed by uncertainty and how much by financing costs.

Japan's record currency intervention had not overcome the wide US-Japan rate gap. OIS assigned about a 78% probability to a near-term BOJ increase, as higher oil raised the import bill and weak yen sustained inflation pressure. More attractive domestic bond yields could also reduce Japanese demand for currency-hedged foreign bonds.

Corporate investment was less robust than profits. Japanese capital expenditure excluding software fell 3.5% from the previous quarter. Including software, spending was flat from a year earlier, against a 4% growth consensus, despite sales rising 1.1% and current profits increasing 14.6%. Profitable companies appeared to be delaying commitments, a risk for domestic demand if policy tightened into more persistent geopolitical uncertainty.

South Korea was trying to ease pressure through bond supply. Finance-ministry officials had held daily calls with dealers and asset managers since May 18, and the government cut planned June issuance by about 21% after the 10-year yield reached its highest since late 2023. After the NY close, May consumer inflation accelerated to 3.1% from 2.6%, exceeding the 2.9% median estimate, while core inflation reached 2.5%. Fuel and travel costs were broadening the price pressure just as the authorities sought to stabilize financing conditions.

China's manufacturing survey offered a partial offset earlier in the window. Its PMI eased to 51.8 from 52.2 as exports weakened, with both input- and output-price inflation slowing. The softer prices contrasted with the renewed pipeline pressure in Europe and the US.

India faced a more direct combination of energy, currency and fiscal risk. Its 10-year sovereign yield had risen about 34 basis points to 7% since the Iran war began; 5-year bonds had lost more as markets priced tightening. A weaker rupee and heavy oil imports increased costs, while fuel and fertilizer subsidies added to public borrowing needs. Kotak Mahindra estimated that revenue shortfalls and higher subsidies could widen the fiscal deficit to 4.6% of GDP, against a 4.3% budget target, or to 4.8% in an adverse case.

Some managers expected 75 to 100 basis points of increases over the cycle, and the 5-year swap had risen more than 60 basis points since the conflict began. Others argued that the supply-led shock called for caution before tightening into weaker demand. The disagreement left shorter and intermediate bonds particularly exposed to oil persistence and currency policy, with the budget consequences extending farther along the sovereign curve.

Turkey's growth slowdown made the trade-off starker. Q1 GDP increased just 0.1% from the preceding quarter, below every estimate and down from 0.4%; annual growth slowed to 2.5% from 3.4%. The central bank had nevertheless raised its year-end inflation target to 24% from 16% because of energy and food costs. Weak growth alone offered limited grounds for easier policy.

Chile showed how quickly the changing oil outlook could affect positioning. Earlier hopes for an agreement had brought long-term breakevens and sovereign risk measures toward pre-war levels and encouraged interest in short nominal peso bonds. The share of investors favoring 1- to 5-year inflation-linked instruments fell to almost 54% from 72% a month earlier. The renewed suspension headlines and oil rebound put that adjustment at risk, depending on the speed of pass-through to fuel and consumer prices.

Colombia's election produced an opposing move. Dollar bonds rose across the curve, the peso gained 3.6%—its strongest day in four years—and swap rates fell after right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella took 43.7% of the first-round vote, ahead of leftist Ivan Cepeda's 40.9%. Both advanced to the runoff. Investors anticipated a more market-friendly policy mix and support for oil development. That political repricing stood out against the broader external backdrop: EMB fell 0.44% as higher US yields, a stronger dollar and more expensive oil weighed on dollar debt and energy importers.

## Forward Market Significance

JOLTS on June 2, ISM services on June 3, claims and revised productivity on June 4, and the employment report on June 5 will show whether manufacturing strength extends across the economy. Openings, hiring and quits will indicate labor demand; services employment and prices will show whether the factory surveys are representative. Payrolls, unemployment, earnings and unit labor costs will help distinguish persistent pressure from the weaker employment detail already evident in manufacturing. Firm demand and services prices would leave the 2- and 5-year sectors exposed to an earlier Fed increase; broader cooling would give investors a reason to reverse some of Monday's repricing.

Oil remains the more immediate source of volatility. A durable restoration of exports through the Strait of Hormuz and sustained crude declines would reduce inflation compensation and give central banks more room to wait. Further disruption would keep oil-importer currencies and bond curves under pressure. The RBI decision on June 5, ECB meeting on June 10-11 and BOJ decision on June 16 will show how officials distinguish temporary energy costs from wider price increases, and whether their responses reinforce the tightening already priced in the US.

Supply will provide a practical test of financing conditions. Treasury has a long-duration buyback on June 3, followed by a front-end cash-management buyback and coupon-supply announcement on June 4. QXO's loan and bond package is expected to progress over June 2-3. Orders near initial terms, stable bills and orderly settlement would show that borrowers can still refinance at the new rate levels. Large corporate concessions or renewed long-bond weakness around the announced 3-, 10- and 30-year supply would point to greater strain on investors' and dealers' capacity.

section_summaries.summary: Oil's rebound and stronger US factories drove a front-end-led Treasury selloff. Corporate funding and equities remained resilient, while energy importers faced renewed inflation pressure alongside pockets of weaker activity.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil and Factory Demand Bring Fed Tightening Closer
section_summaries.summary: An incomplete diplomatic recovery left oil sharply higher. Strong orders and production reinforced expectations of an earlier Fed hike, lifting shorter real yields and inflation compensation while long-term real yields stayed flat.

A downgraded BDC enlarged its bond sale, acquisition and AI borrowers sought funding, and loan scarcity enabled repricing. Atalian required equitization and new senior money; Zambia's tender faced an organized creditor challenge.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil Importers Weigh Inflation Against Weaker Growth
section_summaries.summary: Europe's slowing factories and higher costs illustrated the policy dilemma. Mortgage-sensitive UK housing, Japanese investment and weak Turkish growth added caution, while India's oil and subsidy burden reached into its fiscal outlook. Colombia rallied on election results.

US labor and services releases will test the earlier-hike pricing. Energy flows and overseas policy decisions remain immediate risks, while Treasury operations and QXO's financing will show how supply clears at higher rates.
